title: Founded as Newton Heath LYR
text: Formed by the Carriage and Wagon department of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway depot at Newton Heath, Manchester.

title: Into the Football League
text: After the Football Alliance merged with the Football League, the club started 1892–93 in the First Division. By then it had dropped “LYR” from its name and moved to a new ground at Bank Street.

title: Manchester United
text: The club’s name was changed from Newton Heath to Manchester United.

title: First league title
text: United won the First Division in 1907–08 and began the next season by winning the first ever Charity Shield.

title: First FA Cup
text: Beat Bristol City 1–0 in the final at Crystal Palace, London.

title: Old Trafford opens
text: The stadium’s first match was against Liverpool, who won 4–3. Sandy Turnbull scored the first ever goal at Old Trafford.

title: Matt Busby
text: As football resumed after the war, Busby was appointed manager. He demanded an unprecedented level of control over team selection, transfers and training.

title: FA Cup, 1948
text: A 4–2 win over Blackpool at Wembley, the club’s first major trophy for 37 years.
from_data: Match details: data/club/finals.json (Wikipedia, checked against our match data)

title: Into Europe
text: United became the first English club to compete in the European Cup, despite objections from the Football League. They reached the semi-final, losing to Real Madrid, and beat Anderlecht 10–0, the club’s biggest win on record.

title: Munich
text: The plane carrying the team home from a European Cup tie in Belgrade crashed on its third attempt to take off from Munich-Riem. It claimed 23 lives, including eight players: Geoff Bent, Roger Byrne, Eddie Colman, Duncan Edwards, Mark Jones, David Pegg, Tommy Taylor and Billy Whelan. Busby was hospitalised, and later rebuilt the team.

title: European champions
text: Beat Benfica 4–1 after extra time at Wembley, the first English club to win the European Cup.

title: Relegated
text: United finished 21st in 1973–74 and dropped into the Second Division. They won it at the first attempt, as champions in 1974–75.

title: Banned from Europe
text: English clubs were banned from European competition for five seasons, so United played none between 1985–86 and 1989–90.

title: Alex Ferguson
text: Ferguson joined from Aberdeen on the day the previous manager, Ron Atkinson, was dismissed.

title: 1990 and 1991
text: Reportedly close to the sack after United finished 13th in 1989–90, Ferguson won the FA Cup final replay against Crystal Palace (after a 3–3 draw). The next season United won the Cup Winners’ Cup, beating Barcelona 2–1 in Rotterdam.

title: First league title in 26 years
text: In the first season of the Premier League, 1992–93, United were champions, their first league title since 1966–67.
from_data: Season record: data/club/seasons.json (Wikipedia, checked against the official tables)

title: The Treble
text: United won the Premier League, beat Newcastle 2–0 in the FA Cup final on 22 May 1999, and won the Champions League on 26 May 1999: 1–0 down in injury time against Bayern Munich at the Camp Nou, Teddy Sheringham and Ole Gunnar Solskjær scored late goals. No English club had won all three in one season.

title: Glazer takeover
text: The Glazer family bought a majority shareholding in a deal valuing the club at £800 million, and a month later took it off the London Stock Exchange. In protest, a group of fans formed F.C. United of Manchester.

title: Moscow
text: Champions League winners for the third time: 1–1 with Chelsea at the Luzhniki Stadium, then 6–5 on penalties. Seven months later United won the FIFA Club World Cup, beating LDU Quito 1–0 in Yokohama.

title: Ferguson retires
text: Ferguson announced his retirement after winning a 20th league title, clinched with a 3–0 win over Aston Villa on 22 April 2013. He retired as the most decorated manager in football history.

title: Europa League
text: Beat Ajax 2–0 in Stockholm to win the Europa League, three months after winning the League Cup.

title: New co-owner
text: It was announced that Sir Jim Ratcliffe had purchased 25 per cent of the club, and that his Ineos Sport company was taking control of football operations.

title: FA Cup, 2024
text: Beat Manchester City 2–1 at Wembley for a 13th FA Cup.

title: Bilbao
text: Lost the Europa League final 0–1 to Tottenham Hotspur at San Mamés. That season United finished 15th in the Premier League, their lowest finish since the league began in 1992.
